name: Tawang Monastery
description: Founded in the 17th century, Tawang Monastery is India’s largest Buddhist monastery. Its hilltop complex overlooks the Tawang valley and remains a living centre of Gelugpa Buddhist learning, prayer and art.
how_to_reach: Tawang is reached by road from Tezpur, Guwahati or Bomdila via the Sela corridor. The nearest airports are Tezpur and Salonibari; road conditions and mountain weather should be checked before travel.
practical_notes: Entry is generally free; follow monastery etiquette, dress modestly and ask before photographing prayer halls. October to April usually offers clearer mountain weather. Indian visitors require an Inner Line Permit; foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit. Verify current access rules with Arunachal Tourism before departure.

name: Sela Pass and Sela Lake
description: At roughly 4,170 metres on the route to Tawang, Sela Pass is a dramatic Himalayan crossing surrounded by alpine lakes and snow-bound ridges. Sela Lake is especially striking in clear weather and can be semi-frozen in winter.
how_to_reach: The pass lies on the Bomdila–Dirang–Tawang road. Travel by a reliable high-clearance vehicle with a driver experienced in mountain roads; winter snow and landslides can restrict movement.
practical_notes: There is no standard attraction ticket, but weather, road and permit checks are essential. Carry warm layers, water and altitude medication advice from a clinician if needed. Indian visitors require an ILP and foreign nationals require a PAP.
address: Sela corridor, Tawang district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Bum La Pass
description: Bum La Pass is a high-altitude border pass near the Line of Actual Control, known for sweeping Himalayan views and its demanding approach from Tawang.
how_to_reach: Arrange a local registered vehicle from Tawang. The road is high-altitude and conditions change quickly; access depends on security and weather clearances.
practical_notes: A local permit and security clearance are required in addition to Arunachal entry permits. Carry identification, avoid border photography where restricted and confirm same-day access with local authorities.
entry_fee: Permit and local vehicle charges vary

name: Nuranang Falls (Jung Falls)
description: Nuranang Falls, also called Jung Falls, is a powerful waterfall on the approach to Tawang. It drops through a steep green valley and is most dramatic after the monsoon, when routes can also be more challenging.
how_to_reach: The falls are reached by road from Tawang or Jang on the Tawang–Bomdila route. Use local transport or a hired vehicle and confirm road conditions in the wet season.
practical_notes: Viewing access and local charges can change. Stay behind barriers, wear footwear with grip and avoid slippery rocks. Arunachal entry permits remain mandatory.

name: Tawang War Memorial
description: This stupa-style memorial commemorates Indian soldiers who died in the 1962 conflict. It combines a contemplative memorial setting with views across the Tawang valley.
how_to_reach: Located near Tawang town and reachable by local taxi or private vehicle.
practical_notes: Access hours and ceremony schedules can vary. Maintain a respectful silence and confirm current visiting arrangements locally.

name: Ziro Valley and Apatani Cultural Landscape
description: Ziro is a pine-rimmed plateau of wet-rice fields and Apatani villages. The Apatani Cultural Landscape is on UNESCO’s Tentative List and is recognised for its distinctive agricultural practices, settlement pattern and living cultural heritage.
how_to_reach: Ziro is reached by road from Itanagar or North Lakhimpur. The nearest rail connection is Naharlagun; allow extra time for hilly roads and weather.
practical_notes: October to April is generally comfortable; the Ziro Music Festival is usually held in September and requires advance planning. Respect village privacy and ask before photographing people or homes. ILP/PAP rules apply.
address: Ziro, Lower Subansiri district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Bomdila Monastery
description: Bomdila Monastery is a Tibetan Buddhist complex above the town of Bomdila, visited for its prayer halls, colourful details and views over the Eastern Himalaya.
how_to_reach: Bomdila lies on the Tezpur–Tawang road and is commonly used as an overnight halt before crossing the high pass toward Tawang.
practical_notes: Entry is generally free. Dress modestly and observe quiet prayer spaces. Confirm winter road conditions before travelling onward to Sela Pass.
address: Bomdila, West Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Dirang Valley and Dirang Dzong
description: Dirang is a temperate mountain valley known for orchards, hot springs and its traditional fortified settlement, Dirang Dzong. It is a useful acclimatisation stop on the journey toward Tawang.
how_to_reach: Dirang is on the Tezpur–Bomdila–Tawang route and is reached by shared taxi, bus or hired vehicle from Bomdila and Tezpur.
practical_notes: Hot-spring facilities and village access can change. Visit respectfully, use local guides where offered and check weather conditions before high-altitude onward travel.
address: Dirang, West Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Sangti Valley
description: Sangti Valley is a quiet river valley near Dirang with farm landscapes, pine-covered slopes and seasonal birdlife. It is associated with winter sightings of black-necked cranes, though wildlife movements vary by year.
how_to_reach: Reach Sangti by local vehicle from Dirang. Road conditions can be uneven after heavy rain.
practical_notes: There is no guarantee of crane sightings. Keep a respectful distance from wildlife, avoid drones and confirm local road access before travel.
address: Near Dirang, West Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Mechuka Valley
description: Mechuka is a remote mountain valley near the McMahon Line, shaped by the Siyom River, suspension bridges, grazing country and Tibetan Buddhist heritage. Its isolation makes route planning and weather checks central to the visit.
how_to_reach: Travel by road from Aalo via an extended mountain route; shared taxis and hired 4WD vehicles are common. Plan buffer days for weather and road delays.
practical_notes: Accommodation and fuel options are limited. Carry required permits, cash, warm clothing and offline maps. Border-area access rules can change and must be checked locally.
address: Mechuka, Shi Yomi district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Samten Yongcha Monastery
description: Samten Yongcha Monastery is an old Buddhist monastery in the Mechuka region, visited for its contemplative setting and long connection to Himalayan Buddhist traditions.
how_to_reach: Reach the monastery by local vehicle or on foot from the Mechuka area; ask locally about the current approach road.
practical_notes: Treat the monastery as an active religious place. Ask before photography, avoid disturbing rituals and check local access conditions.
address: Mechuka area, Shi Yomi district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Namdapha National Park and Tiger Reserve
description: Namdapha is one of India’s largest protected areas, spanning tropical lowland forest to high Himalayan habitats. The park is notable for exceptional biodiversity and records of tiger, leopard, snow leopard and clouded leopard, though wildlife sightings are never guaranteed.
how_to_reach: The main gateway is Miao in Changlang district, reached by road from Dibrugarh or Tinsukia. Continue with registered local transport and park arrangements.
practical_notes: Park entry, guide and accommodation permissions must be arranged in advance. Follow forest department rules, avoid single-use plastic and never approach wildlife. ILP/PAP requirements apply.
entry_fee: Forest entry, guide and stay charges apply
address: Miao gateway, Changlang district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Ita Fort
description: Ita Fort is a large brick fortification in Itanagar, generally dated to the 14th–15th centuries. Its name means “fort of bricks” and its surviving walls make it a key archaeological landmark of the capital region.
how_to_reach: Located in Itanagar and accessible by local taxi or auto-rickshaw from the city centre and Naharlagun railhead.
practical_notes: Access arrangements and site conditions can change. Wear suitable shoes for uneven ground and respect any protected-monument restrictions.
address: Itanagar, Papum Pare district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Golden Pagoda, Namsai
description: The Golden Pagoda is a Theravada Buddhist complex in Namsai, designed in a Thai-Burmese-inspired style and set within landscaped grounds. It reflects the Buddhist heritage of Arunachal’s eastern plains.
how_to_reach: Namsai is reached by road from Dibrugarh, Tinsukia or Tezu. Local taxis connect the town and pagoda complex.
practical_notes: Dress modestly, remove footwear where directed and confirm ceremony timings locally. Entry and photography rules can vary during religious events.

name: Parashuram Kund
description: Parashuram Kund is a revered pilgrimage site on the Lohit River in the Mishmi hills. It attracts large gatherings around Makar Sankranti and is valued for both its spiritual significance and dramatic river setting.
how_to_reach: Reach by road from Tezu; the final approach and river conditions should be confirmed locally, especially during festival periods or heavy rain.
practical_notes: Makar Sankranti draws heavy crowds and requires advance accommodation planning. Follow river safety instructions and respect local religious practices. ILP/PAP requirements apply.
entry_fee: Free; festival transport and local services vary
address: Near Tezu, Lohit district, Arunachal Pradesh

name: Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi)
description: Ganga Lake, also known as Gyakar Sinyi, is a forest-fringed lake outside Itanagar. Its still water and surrounding greenery make it a short nature break from the capital area.
how_to_reach: The lake is reached by local taxi or private vehicle from Itanagar. Confirm the approach-road condition during the monsoon.
practical_notes: Boating and site facilities can vary. Avoid littering, follow local safety signage and check opening details before setting out.
address: Near Itanagar, Papum Pare district, Arunachal Pradesh
